physicalDetails.detail: Wears leathers and a longbow/quiver; green and gold colours at her shoulder (read by the prisoner). Right hand habitually bare for touching stones, glove pulled off then back on.
Rides a fine-boned mare that has stood beside a hundred ward-stones. Tall enough that a seated prisoner must tip her head back when Sylvanas stands in front of the chair.
Lay in wet bracken long enough to soak both knees and one elbow; knees remind her how long she has lain.

In the cell: the ward-lamp behind her throws her shadow over the prisoner's knees and boots; green and gold at her shoulder gone dark. Smells of horse, cold air, crushed fern. Seen from Jaina's POV as the one who looks at a mouth, not the eyes, 'the way a hunter watches a gap in the brush'; her face 'stayed shut'.

Rides a fine-boned Thalassian mare that tosses her head at the cold; sits straight in green and gold; carries bow in her left hand and kept an arrow on the string for much of the road. Knelt in ditch water without noticing to cut the doe open.

Chapter 3 (first time inside her POV since Ch1): eyes 'full of sand', breeches wet at the knees from the ditch, the doe's blood dried brown in her knuckles; has not slept since the night before the troll hollow. By the morning ride she sees the road 'go very flat and very bright' and is 'not far behind' the sleeping mage. Wears a signet ring with a leaf-and-arrow device (sealing wax: it blurred on one side). Carries a belt knife and a worn stub of lead in a belt pouch. Uses her teeth to pull her right glove off at the cut.

Chapter 4 (seen from Jaina): taller than Brask and 'made nothing of it'; green cloak, bare head, bow on her back; right hand bare 'as always', left glove worn. By dusk the left glove is grey with flour, worked into the seams and smeared on the green of her cuff where she wiped it and made it worse. At night the cloak smells of scorched flour and smoke. Two of her bare fingers carry deep teeth marks from Tam's bite (she wipes them on her coat). Glimpsed through the chapel's bubble-glass window bent thin and tall.

Chapter 5 (back in her own POV): eyes 'rubbed with sand', has not slept since the night before the village; knees 'set in the shape of the saddle' and stiff for the first steps after dismounting (worse at the river depot, 'set again in the night'); the two fingers Tam bit are purple at the middle joint and slow to bend (stiff on the bowstring, she closes them); right hand habitually flat to her coat over the folded sacking. Fingers and gloves blacked with ink and ash all chapter ('ash-black finger'); gloves left by her boot 'blacking everything they touched'. Bare right palm on the wagon-board bench. Slept once in the saddle on the river night, a moment, waking with her hand already at the bowstring. Carries in her coat: the ANDORHAL sacking square, Corley's copied list, the big folded sheet (folded 'wrong' on new creases), later the burned-depot slips. Belt knife used to pin the word Strahnbrad into the bench.

Chapter 6 (seen from Jaina's POV, no interior): rides in front with her back straight and her bow lying across the saddle; keeps it 'easy across her saddle' during talk. Face still when she hears Jaina out; looks Jaina over once (crystal, hand on the reins) and returns to her face. Sits motionless at the crest reading the camp 'from one end to the other'. Gets down at the hedge, takes the map sheet out of her coat folded small with the slips and the sacking tucked in, holds it up to Jaina's stirrup; later pushes the slips back, folds it small and puts it away inside her coat. Puts her horse across the tally-man's path. Turns all the way round in the saddle, one hand flat on her horse's rump. Her horse scrapes her boot along a wall when it shies; she calms it low and steady in Thalassian with a hand flat on its neck. Greeted by Arthas with a small correct bow from the neck.

Chapter 7 (own POV): stands in the gate queue on foot, the low sun flat across the back of her neck, legs stiff from the saddle. Writes the pass on the lid of the ostler's feed bin with his pen and seals it with the leaf-and-arrow pressed into wax softened at his lamp. Tall elf (an 'elf standing alone at the end of an empty lane' would be seen at once). The two fingers Tam bit catch the roof edge late and hold badly: she puts her weight on the other two and her forearm and climbs anyway, heart going hard for a short climb. By the end soot blackens both sleeves to the cuff, grit on her cheek and soot smeared when she rubs it with her wrist. Carries the folded sheet from the south road (Jaina's blots over her own lines), Brask's square of sacking in her coat, a lead stub, and a belt knife.

voiceMarkers.detail: Clipped commands and short replies: 'Do.', 'Down.', 'Skip the compliments. What.', 'Inside. Report as we go.', 'Open it.', 'Start talking.'
Dry deflection with Lor'themar ('Then he can come south and break one.', 'Wouldn't miss it.'). Tactical metaphors drawn from tracking, horses, hounds and troll behaviour.

Interior voice is blunt and self-interrogating: runs sequences of 'Or...' hypotheses, swears privately ('Damn them. And damn her too', 'Sun's sake', 'Damn the old man, and Dalaran, and every tower in it').
Never says 'Jaina' even in thought; the prisoner is 'the mage', 'the human', 'the prisoner' / 'the girl' (file memory). She hears the name from Cyndia but does not adopt it.

Chapter 2 (heard only through Jaina): minimal and level, 'the same pitch as everything else': 'Go on.', 'Which stones read worst. Where.', 'Most.', 'Horses.', 'Up.', 'Then she eats in the saddle.', 'Take her.', 'Millhaven.', 'Not on the hill.', 'Hold.', 'Is it in my horses?', 'Then I pick the ground.' Uses the voice she uses for horses when she corrects Jaina ('Your lines don't spread'). When she needs to she goes loud ('*Front!*') and the command cracks off the hedges. Gives no praise: no 'better', no 'that's more like it'.

States terms flatly in a list ('You ride inside my escort. Your hands stay where a ranger can see them...'), and agrees with Jaina's one remark with a cold truth ('No. You wouldn't.'). Calls the mage 'Mage', once 'Proudmoore'.

Chapter 3 aloud: procedural and short ('Down.', 'Houses first.', 'Then it will still be here when we've opened the doors.', 'Count.', 'Then don't guess.', 'Keep on.', 'Mount.', 'South.'). Gives orders in lists with prohibitions ('nobody stands in a doorway with the light behind them'). Speaks to the child only once and badly ('Which is the north road?' flat, in the common tongue; the girl flinches) and otherwise hands the child to Neral and speaks Thalassian over her head. Dry cruelty about the Convocation in her head ('Let him count it. She had sixty in a cow way.'). Honest refusal to guess aloud: 'I don't know. Not on this ground. Not in the dark.'

Chapter 3 interior: short imperative self-checks ('Don't. Find out.', 'Don't make them into the doe because it's late and you want a story to put on it.', 'Leave it.'), rhetorical questions ('What drill did she have for a drawknife set down tidy?', 'Who drives sixty dead up a cow way in the dark?'), 'Sun's sake' and 'Damn her, then' / 'Damn.' as private swearing. Similes from hunting and herding (hare under a hawk, sheep through a gap, bellwether, herd milling in a clearing). Interior uses 'the mage' throughout (never 'Jaina'), 'Proudmoore' only aloud at the well, 'the prisoner' in status thoughts.

Chapter 4 (heard through Jaina): the second register she has with civilians: LOW, level and plain, 'a woman telling him how far it was to the next ford', pitched for one man's ear so the crowd cannot hear; no raised voice. Concedes first ('You're right to stop us.'), gives the facts in order and with objects (the cradle, the spoon in the bowl, 'we counted their prints'), then one brief, even question-shaped lever ('Your people are watching you, Captain... Keep your spear. Walk with me.'). Offers a bet on her own honesty ('Then let my mage see your sick, and we'll know by dark whether I'm a liar.'). With Jaina keeps the ledger voice: 'Mage. What you find, I want before dark.', 'Well, mage?', 'How sure?', 'Can you leave them?', 'Then we're quick.', 'Mage. Will it hold?', 'Mage. Up.' Short clipped assent: 'On purpose.' to Jaina's half-sentence. Dry sarcasm about the keeper's description ('I asked him for a face. He gave me a young man with a cart.'). To Brask: 'Then you have until cockcrow.'

Chapter 5 aloud: lists and one-word tasking ('Cyndia. The yard and the gate. Count the carts and anything chalked on that scale. Lyriel, with me.', 'Count the short-rate lines by road. Before the last month and since.', 'The first short-rate load on each road. The date.', 'Back.', 'No.'). Bargains with a clerk by laying out the evidence ('Show me your book, Master Corley, and I'll show you the sacking...'); invokes her office plainly ('the Ranger-General of Quel'Thalas has them, and he can write to Silvermoon'). To Jaina: 'Mage.' (twice), then 'Proudmoore. Read him.' and 'Proudmoore. Barov.' as work-commands; refuses Jaina's offer of a re-read with a flat 'No.'; the one concession: 'You'll have to. I can't see it either.' Gives an exact tactical briefing at the fork (King's road clean and drained, the south road is the one the grain comes up, the army is on it). Interior: 'Damn the paper.', 'Sun's sake, she wanted it.', 'Not yet. Who had the key to this place? Start there.', self-correcting rhetorical questions, and long strings of 'Or...' hypotheses; self-sarcasm ('been pleased with herself for thinking it'). Interior names the mage 'the mage' until the fork scene, then 'Jaina' (see nameUsagePatterns).

Chapter 6 aloud (heard through Jaina): one-word challenges and level commands. 'Somebody.' (testing Jaina's phrasing), 'And when you say that to a man who can't feel any of it?', 'Paper. He'll have clerks for paper.', 'He has orcs in his hills, Mage. Make it short.' To the sergeant, formal and exact: 'Ranger-General Sylvanas Windrunner, of Quel'Thalas. Proudmoore rides under my escort.' To Arthas, his title said perfectly level: 'Your Highness.' Her call, aimed at Arthas's back while he can still prove her wrong, delivered to Jaina: 'He's going to write to his father, Proudmoore, and then he's going back up that hill.' After: 'Give it here, Mage.'; the verdict: 'He's a good commander, with an enemy he can see and men who'd follow him into it. He'll fight that war, and likely win it.' 'And the other one?' / 'Is ours.' To the tally-man: 'You've come from Andorhal.' 'Who runs the granaries?' Then: 'Mage. Did you read anything off him?', 'The blessing. I had the same one at Millhaven, from an old carter going north over the bridge.', 'Once, it's a farewell. Twice, it's wrong. That's as far as it goes yet.' Asks for no history, gives no thanks, no warmth.

Chapter 7 aloud: short questions that work as orders ('Where are people sick, Captain?', 'Is it?', 'Since when?', 'The loaders.', 'Why haven't you taken them?', 'Are those your loaders, Captain?', 'Who stands over them in the yard?', 'Show me Hurdle Lane.'); one-word or two-word commands to her pack ('Inside.', 'Tonight.', 'Keep them there.', 'Cyndia. The roofs over the back lane...', 'Lyriel. The bend in Tenter Row...'). Orders by event, not by counted time ('When the Exchange rings the night shift.', 'You don't loose until I call.'). Aloud always finished and sure: 'I have the hands.', 'That's mine.', 'I'll find my own.', 'Stay behind Proudmoore.' Interior: short semicolon clauses and tallies, sour and exact ('She'd have had the rope-walk shut the first night.', 'Leave it in the wall. Take the man.'); no feelings named.

beliefs.belief: South of the wards is Lordaeron's business and none of hers unless it comes over her line.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Being overturned: the stone and the mage put the south on her ledger. In chapter 2 she leads a ride into it. Chapter 3: she chooses, from the inside, to keep riding south after the border is warned.

beliefs.belief: Magisters never put a bare hand on a ward-stone; their wardens, lenses and clerks write 'stable' and the signatures are trusted over hands-on knowledge.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Open. The stone in her palm contradicts three signed reports.

beliefs.belief: Kirin Tor masters breed arrogance into apprentices; she expects a court-polished prisoner with a sealed letter held back to do harm.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: False for this prisoner: Jaina is road-worn, frost-bitten and furious.

beliefs.belief: A spy runs; frightened people run. A person who sits down before a drawn bow and asks to be tied to a stone is arrogant, mad, or right.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Resolving toward 'right': by the end of chapter 2 she has ridden south on the mage's word and acts on her map. Chapter 3: she waits for the mage's read before refusing to guess, and the mage's sorting of the prints produces the count.

beliefs.belief: The mage's contamination lines can be checked on the map: ruled south and off the edge they close at the Millhaven crossroads.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Inferred from her correction of Jaina; she says it plainly. 'Most of them cross within a mile of the Millhaven crossroads. The rest miss it by less than the width of your pen.'

beliefs.belief: Deer do not run at horses, and wolves do not hunt beside deer; whatever drove them was not hunger or fear of a predator.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Confirmed by Cyndia's tracking: deer and wolf in one track, nothing chasing anything.

beliefs.belief: A town does not simply stop; the people of Millhaven did not flee (a fleeing village takes coats, bread, the cow, a child's toy) and were not taken (every door whole, no hoofprints): 'Or they had got up and walked out.'
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Confirmed on the ground by the clog, the lane, the girl and the drove way.

beliefs.belief: A child's word through a cellar grating is not enough to send a border warning on; the ground has to match the testimony. She would 'have had the hide off any ranger who sent a warning on that'.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Held. The cut at first light supplies the ground; she holds the warning overnight and sends it only then.

beliefs.belief: The loudest place in a village is where the herd milled about, 'never where the herd came in' (her reading of the granary reading loudest).
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Sylvanas's own analogy for why she accepts Jaina's refusal to call the storehouse the source; she does not conclude 'grain'.

beliefs.belief: Elves cannot feel the contamination: 'Nothing in the hide or the bones of her hand. There never was.' Wrongness reaches her only through horses, silence, the staff and the mage.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Consistent with Ch2 world/magic.

beliefs.belief: The carter's 'May the stars keep your road' is some hill saying, a carter's grandmother's; 'Light keep you' or 'Safe road' is what humans say, or nothing at all. 'Leave it.'
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Plan-level plant: she is meant to be wrong or at least incurious. Not resolved on page.

beliefs.belief: She is following 'the trail', not the mage: 'No. On the trail. The read was the trail; it was the only trail there was.'
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Self-deception marker for the partnership arc: she is in fact riding south on a human prisoner's read.

beliefs.belief: A frightened armed man at a spear must be given his dignity and an audience: lower the voice, hand over the bow, concede the point, then ask him to walk with you so his people see him with you.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Works on Brask; seen by Jaina as a skill she 'could it be learned?'

beliefs.belief: Walk the supply, not the sick: go to the granary and bakehouse first and ask what it costs, who brings it, since when and who else buys it.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Works; she reaches the new man's flour from the other end while Jaina reaches it through the patients. (Jaina cannot say how she got there 'by some road of her own'.)

beliefs.belief: The flour is being sold to them on purpose; the young man with the cart is the carrier (the same 'new man' as Millhaven).
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Finishes Jaina's sentence aloud: 'On purpose.' Confirmed by the lookout and the poison jar.

beliefs.belief: A live witness is worth more than the safe way to take one: she acts at once to stop a lookout dying (fingers in his mouth) although it costs her the bite and does not work.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Fails (Tam dies); Sylvanas reads it as taught behaviour: 'Somebody taught him that. They sewed it in for him and told him when.'

beliefs.belief: She is following one man, a young man with a cart.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Broken in chapter 5 at Corley's: thirty-one short-rate places in one book, forty-seven then fifty-three slips across four roads: 'One man with a cart didn't sell grain short at forty-odd villages on four roads in one season. That was somebody with yards and books and boys.' The cart man is now an agent, not the author.

beliefs.belief: A slow hunt always runs a day behind; bad luck, a free carter's hours.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Abandoned in the wood: someone is a day ahead every time (the miller's buy-back, the ostler's southbound carter, Corley's east road), 'shutting doors, or behind her reading the road... and sending word on'. Open: informant or foresight, unproven.

beliefs.belief: She can lay Jaina's marks against paper and check them.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Partly true and partly not: 'So far, every mark she could lay against a book had matched it.' But the south-road verdict cannot be checked ('she was going to put four horses on a road she could not check') and she goes anyway.

beliefs.belief: A frightened man's fast answers (the overseer) are a lie to be got round, but a fast answer costs a breath she cannot spare; the wagons are getting further off.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: False: she took a frightened man's word 'in a warm room because the wagons were getting further off', rode a day north on the Brill road for nothing; she names it the same excuse she once flayed a ranger for. She reads the stove ash (fresh, still glowing) as Corley's kettle and misses it until too late.

beliefs.belief: The overseer was told when and what to burn.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Suspected only: 'A frightened man doesn't pick what to put in the stove... Or he does, if somebody told him what to pick.' She does not know who.

beliefs.belief: The Barov name on the paper means connection, not proof of guilt: 'if Barov held the granaries, his name was on every sack... rotten or sound.' She wants it to be him ('Sun's sake, she wanted it') and holds herself back.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Unknown. Honest uncertainty held; a ranger who brought her only a name would be sent back for more.

beliefs.belief: The old carter's empty wagon going north was one odd old man on a road ('Everybody stares at elves too long').
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Reopened but unmatched: the bench of wagon boards (grain dust packed in the cracks) makes her recall his empty, grain-dusty wagon, 'Nothing for me here, then', and that he drove north, not away, and asked after the young man with the cart. She tries him beside the depot and beside the cart man and he fits neither, 'except that he had asked after him.' 'An empty wagon, going the wrong way.' Filed, not concluded.

beliefs.belief: Kirin Tor mages want their work admired; the mage will want the 'wasn't that something'.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Dissolving: after Jaina's reads proved out she waits 'for the bit at the end' and the woman is 'picking frost off her finger, reading the map upside down'; and Jaina moves her own marks without pride (Hollow Green, Ashford). Sylvanas thinks 'Jaina, then.'

beliefs.belief: The army will rank the flour after the orcs; Arthas will write to his father and go back up the hill.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: CONFIRMED at Strahnbrad. She said it at the fork (Ch5) and to his face before Jaina finished.

beliefs.belief: Arthas is 'a good commander, with an enemy he can see and men who'd follow him into it'; the plague war 'is ours'.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Her verdict, stated without contempt. Human command will fight the visible war; the party fights the other.

beliefs.belief: A farewell once is a farewell; the same farewell twice, from a different stranger on the road, is wrong. She cannot say more than that yet.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Open. She states the limit herself ('That's as far as it goes yet'). She also relies on Jaina's sense and gets 'nothing but a tired clerk'.

beliefs.belief: A trained man's stillness is a tell: eight placed at corner, trough, platform and gate are the same kind as Tam on the hoist (trained waiting, not fatigue). They will not talk (Brask's boy had his death sewn into his collar; these will have the same).
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Supported by the yard; not yet tested. Sets up the capture's death-curse question for Ch8.

beliefs.belief: Do not touch the dead drop: pull the thing from the crack and the next man finds an empty crack and the eight are gone by morning with the locks and the factor. Leave it in the wall; take the man.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Her tactical call; not yet tested.

beliefs.belief: Havel's lane-steering fits a territorial captain who keeps strangers on his own streets, or someone who wants her off Tenter Row; she cannot tell which. She admits she has no better reason to doubt him than that he is slow and she is sick of slow men.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Unresolved; both readings must hold until Ch8.

beliefs.belief: The sample room and the mage quarter need Jaina and not a bow in a corridor; Jaina can read bags and she cannot read drilled men's walks.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Vindicated: Jaina's read maps onto Sylvanas's roof sighting; the raid exists only because both halves exist.

beliefs.belief: The cell thinks the city is theirs and will leave one man coming and going alone through a door tonight; by first light they will not need to. A live prisoner has to be taken tonight, partly because she is sick of arriving a day late.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Her operational call; outcome in Ch8.

goalsAtChapterEnd.active: Take one living man out of Kett's loft tonight while the shift is still sewing; Cyndia on the roofs across from the loft, Lyriel at the bend in Tenter Row, Jaina close enough to touch the man, Havel's lads held at the Hurdle Lane end.
goalsAtChapterEnd.underlying: Stop arriving a day late (the swept depot, the cold stove, the smiling overseer); learn who sits above the eight and the masked five; keep Jaina alive through one more use of her hands.

goalsAtChapterEnd_chapter6.active: Reach the market gate and the militia post; ask for Captain Havel as the tally-man said; get into Andorhal with the four riders and the evidence in her coat. (Outside view only; inferred from her acts.)
goalsAtChapterEnd_chapter6.underlying: The farewell twice: find out who is passing the same words along the road, and who warned the doors ahead of her. Keep Jaina on her horse. (Inferred.)

goalsAtChapterEnd_chapter5.active: Ride the south road into the hills toward Strahnbrad on Jaina's read and Cyndia's army-wagon tracks, then on to Andorhal by the back way; get Jaina to show the army the flour when they block the road.
goalsAtChapterEnd_chapter5.underlying: Find whoever sits behind the lord's granaries, the overseer, the boys and the paper (the Barov name is a lead, not a verdict); stop being a day behind; reach one door before the doorkeeper is warned. Keep the Brill-road error from costing another day.

goalsAtChapterEnd_chapter4.active: Follow the grain road south and west to Andorhal after the young man with the cart; keep Jaina in the line; reach the supplier's source before more villages bake with it.
goalsAtChapterEnd_chapter4.underlying: Find the person who builds and distributes it; stop it spreading before it reaches her ward line from another direction; keep telling herself she follows the trail, not the mage (not shown this chapter; inferred from Ch3).
goalsAtChapterEnd_chapter4.note: Seen only from outside in chapter 4 (Jaina POV): no interior.

goalsAtChapterEnd_chapter3.active: Ride south down the valley with three rangers and the mage, following the contamination toward the settlements that are still alive.
goalsAtChapterEnd_chapter3.underlying: Find out what drove sixty dead up a cow way and what is spreading south, before it reaches her ward line from another direction; keep the mage (the only one who can say which way to ride) under her control.

emotionalStateAtChapterEnd.state: Own POV: hard, narrow and sick of slow men; the field confidence of the gate gone (a city with more paper than weak points); an unvoiced unease at Havel she sets beside her own admitted bias; a plain, unspoken reliance on Jaina (she worried that Jaina would be 'white by the time the bell went', and Jaina backing her before she asked is noticed and not mentioned); and a strained sense of spreading her people thin ('so thin she could see light through it').

emotionalStateAtChapterEnd_chapter6.state: Outside view only: level and unsmug after being proved right; turned toward the city and waiting for Jaina's word at the crest ('Sylvanas turned to her and waited'); a sharpened wariness over the farewell she cannot yet use.

emotionalStateAtChapterEnd_chapter5.state: Second night(s) without sleep; hard, narrow and self-angry over the Brill-road day lost to a stove and a polite liar; grudging, quiet respect for Jaina (thinks 'Jaina, then') that she will not voice; wary under it because she is staking four horses on a read she cannot verify; a sour new unease at the scale of the network and the nagging empty wagon. Ends on the road south at dawn with a brown moving smear over the hills.

emotionalStateAtChapterEnd_chapter4.state: Outwardly the same: composed, quick, short. Seen only from outside: she stands a long moment at the cage and then on her knees in the straw with her fingers in a dying boy's teeth; stays on the threshold at midnight to report; very late and unthanked she is in the doorway smelling of smoke. She takes Jaina's thanks without reply. No interior shown.

emotionalStateAtChapterEnd_chapter3.state: Exhausted, flat-bright with sleeplessness; tightly controlled; uneasy at the gaps she has put in her own line (two empty places, 'she had sent them back up the road herself'); resents carrying a human problem; keeps telling herself it is the trail and not the mage; the carter's farewell has already been filed as 'leave it'.

decisionsThisChapter.detail: Chose to extend the patrol south to check the ward-stones rather than turn home (stalling the Convocation).
Kept the cold-stone finding to herself after Lor'themar deflected it to the magisters; told him only 'It's off.'
Split the party at the fork: Lor'themar and patrol north to Silvermoon; she rides on with the runner to the Pass.
Refused to hand the prisoner to a magister; entered the cell and opened with 'Start talking.'

In the cell: let Jaina talk, then questioned her narrowly (why alone, which stones, where, how far, where do the lines come up from); ordered Cyndia to fetch horses; set terms; then took Jaina south to test her claim on the ground instead of holding her for a magister. (Cyndia pulled the damper wedge from behind the chair as the party left; no explicit order is shown.)
Named Millhaven as the destination; assigned positions (Proudmoore in the middle, Lyriel right, Cyndia shoulder, Neral behind with the grey, fourth ranger rear); named Neral relay.

Refused Jaina's first request to stop ('Not on the hill'), then granted the culvert halt ('Here. Water them. Proudmoore. You wanted the road.'); called Jaina three times when she went under; ringed her with the escort while she was down.
Corrected Jaina's model on the move ('Your lines don't spread') from her own reading of the map; answered Jaina's source-or-sink plan with 'Then I pick the ground.'
Ordered 'Leave her' about the bawling cow; sent Cyndia to check the farmhouse; ordered 'On.'
Led the ambush defence: shot the lead doe, assigned Lyriel the stag and Cyndia the left, called every move; ran roll-call after.
Ordered Jaina off the road into the ditch to read the doe; opened the doe with her own knife at Jaina's direction; asked about the horses; asked where it was strongest.
Ordered a hard ride; if Jaina's horse falls she stays with it and Lyriel returns for her; if the grey goes lame, cut him loose.
On the crest: ordered a slow walk in, bows in hand, Cyndia left, Lyriel right, Jaina in the middle.

Held the mare through the spook and ordered a procedural split at the crossing: Neral and the horses to the inn yard; the fourth ranger to the bridge ('Nothing comes over it from either side till I call'); Cyndia and Lyriel to sweep the east side in pairs ('nobody stands in a doorway with the light behind them'); she took the west side alone with the mage kept at her side, hands in sight. Refused Jaina's request to read the crossing first ('Houses first.').

Only after the houses: chose the ground for the well read ('She would not have put a sick mage on her knees there for any money in Silvermoon, not without cover'), put Lyriel on the inn gallery, Cyndia at the smithy corner, the fourth ranger on the bridge, and herself back to the well-head. Hauled the bucket herself. Called the mage out of the read ('Mage', 'Proudmoore', '*Proudmoore!*'), then dragged her hand off the frozen cobbles by the wrist.

Forbade the mage to read with her hands any more that night ('You're done reading with those tonight'), took the staff for a moment and found nothing in it but a stick and a tremor; took Jaina's refusal to call the storehouse the source and did not argue it.

Refused to call a direction from the lane in the dark ('I don't know. Not on this ground. Not in the dark.') even though 'north' was what she wanted to say; ordered every cellar, loft, oven, chest and chimney-breast searched for a living witness.
Stayed above the hatch with an arrow on the string while Neral talked the girl out, and sent the mage down only to say what else was in the cellar; gave the child to Neral and stood in the doorway.

Questioned the girl's route through Thalassian instructions to Neral ('Ask her how she knows which way. She was under the floor.'), then spoke to her directly once ('Which is the north road?'), frightening her. Found the cellar slot herself and confirmed the line of sight.

Held the warning overnight ('That's enough tonight'; Neral told 'At first light... When I've seen the cow way.'), set the watch (Lyriel and the fourth ranger, then Cyndia and herself, Neral exempt), had Cyndia wrap the mage's hands, and sat the gallery past her own watch.

At first light inspected the open gate and the drove way, read the grooves by bare fingertip and depth against her knuckle, used the mage and Cyndia to separate heavy marks from cattle, hunted the cut for a single leader and found none, then called the count and the direction ('Sixty... north-northeast, toward the outer ring east of the Pass. Not our road.').

Wrote the dispatch to Lor'themar in Thalassian: Millhaven dead, five days at most, no bodies, sixty and more walked out north-northeast by a drove way east of the road toward the ring between the Pass and the eastern posts; double the wardens and put eyes on the high ground; the Pass road south is clear; a human child witness is coming with the courier; 'I am going on south.' Sealed it with her leaf-and-arrow ring (blurred) and gave it to Neral for Lor'themar's hand.

Stripped her own party to four to guarantee the warning and the child reach the Pass; kept the mage with her because she is a prisoner and 'you did not hand a Kirin Tor apprentice to a relay rider with a child on her saddle'. Re-formed the walking order ('Same as the crest... I have the front').

Told the carter at the bridge: 'Dead. Five days. Don't water your horse here, and don't touch the well.' Asked him where he had come from and who was still trading; did not draw on him; did not question the farewell.

Chose to ride on south rather than fall back, though 'her duty was done, by any measure the chamber would put its seal to'; let the mage sleep in the saddle and watered at noon only when she woke; rode the afternoon down the valley toward the first living farm.

Chapter 4: halted the party at Brask's spear, got down without hurry, handed her bow up to Cyndia and walked up unarmed; conceded his right to stop them, told him Millhaven in detail (laid tables, the cradle, no one living or dead, sixty prints, a child alive in a cellar who said it began with everybody coughing at the well); offered him the test of her mage by dark; asked him to walk his village with her so his people would see him with her. Sent Lyriel with Jaina, Cyndia with herself.

Went directly to the long stone granary and the bakehouse (supply, not the sick); questioned the keeper (Joss) and baker (Hob): price, supplier, since when, who else buys; took a pinch of flour from a sack, rubbed it, wrote on a scrap against the doorpost, later wrote the baker's numbers. Glanced up at the chapel window.

At dusk came to the chapel and asked 'Well, mage?'; had Cyndia report; asked 'How sure?', 'How much of his flour is left?', 'Can you leave them?'; ordered nobody takes another sack from the loft; led the party to the granary and tried to leave Jaina by the water butt; allowed her in behind her own heels when Jaina lifted the staff.

In the loft: ordered 'Put it down'; when Tam went for the lamp, loosed an arrow through the loose sleeve of his smock above the wrist into the post behind him, took the lamp, wound the wick to a bead, set it on a sack, ground out the burning oil with her boot; later set Lyriel and Cyndia to cut him loose; asked Brask for somewhere that locks.

At the cage questioned Tam ('Who gives you the jar? ... Who brings the flour?'); when he convulsed she took the key from Brask, went in, put her bare fingers into his mouth and tried to hook out the poison (bitten to the teeth marks); found the waxed-paper fold sewn into the collar hem; concluded someone taught him and told him when.

Accepted Jaina's warning and gave Brask the deadline ('Then you have until cockcrow') in the same low voice she used at the spear; after Brask agreed went after him without waiting. Came once very late, on the threshold, to say the granary and bakehouse were burned, houses mostly done, the cart not back, the loft untouched ('His sacks came down round your ice, one at a time, with Brask's man calling the steps').

Before the fire took the loft sacks, cut a square of stencilled sacking (sheaf of wheat in a ring, 'ANDORHAL') with her knife and pocketed it; showed it to Jaina and Brask in the morning; folded it away when Jaina doubted the clue ('Either way, it's the road he drove.'); had her name written in Brask's ledger, spelled flat and clear; turned the mare onto the grain road south and west without a word.

Chapter 5 day 1: led the depot search (sent Cyndia to the yard, took Lyriel into the office, parked Jaina at the crossing to read); leveraged Lyriel's chat plus the sacking to get Corley to open the out-book; found 'own cart' short-rate lines; with Jaina drew the roads and marks on Corley's waybill paper (Millhaven top north road, the sick village where the west road bends, unnamed); had Cyndia count short-rate loads by road before/since last month (north 9/3, west 7/4, south 11/6, east 1/9) and the first dates; had Corley copy out the 31 short-rate lines (Cyndia sat with him); took the list.

Chapter 5 day 2: slept in the carters' inn loft (took first and second watch); went the stops: miller past Coldwell, hamlet shop with notch-stick, Wick stable book, second depot clerk (south road) who named the big depot down the river road as the breaking point; built the table at a south-road inn (47 places, 19 in more than one book); heard two men in good brown coats say the King's army and Prince Arthas are at Strahnbrad after orcs; refused the Plough and rode through the night; watered at the Plough only.

Chapter 5 day 3 (river depot): arrived grey dawn at an empty swept three-barn depot; interviewed the overseer in the office (he lied smoothly: books gone to the regional office, grain sold whole to Tolliver and Sons, Brill, six wagons north two days ago); had Jaina read him (nothing on him); let him go uninterrogated because 'every breath in this room was a furlong'; rode the Brill road north at a canter.

Chapter 5 afternoon: read the slumped ruts on the clay hill (no cut edges after the rain), had Cyndia confirm, spoke to the toll-keeper via Lyriel (no grain on this road in over a month; a company of King's foot cutting across), realised 'there had never been any wagons', turned the party back ('Back.') with the sunset behind them; rode the second night without sleep; the mage's mare went down on the causeway.

Chapter 5 dawn 4: went over the wall of the shut depot; found the house abandoned in haste (drawers out, shawl dropped, trap and horse gone, washing on the line); the bridge-keeper saw the overseer and his crying wife go south at a trot yesterday; knelt to the stove and found burned waybill halves, parchment with 'Barov', broken red seals; had Cyndia bring the ash-pit in a bucket; laid scraps in rows like arrowheads; with Cyndia, counted 53 readable slips each with Andorhal at one end, 9 more burned through; fanned them with the ANDORHAL sacking at the narrow end.

Chapter 5 midnight at the fork carters' lodge: took the slips out in bundles and read each place and date to Jaina for a one-word read (Heavy/Light/Old/Starting/Nothing); concluded grain went everywhere out of Andorhal but the heavy/old marks cluster on the south road; asked Jaina which road: staff leaned toward the south bend; made Ashford heavy at Jaina's correction; wrote Strahnbrad at the end of the south road on the bench and pinned it with her belt knife; refused Jaina's offered re-read at dawn; briefed 'Expect them to get in the way'; turned the mare south onto the bending road.

Chapter 6: stopped to hear Jaina's plain line and tested it ('Somebody.'; the 'show it' problem); told her to make it short because Arthas has orcs; read the Strahnbrad camp and named the command tent, the riders, the doubled east pickets and the one sergeant and a hedge on the road side; led the party down at a walk; spoke to the sergeant and gave her own rank and name; got down and handed Jaina the evidence; stayed behind Jaina during the audience, then called Arthas's decision aloud in front of him; took the paper back and put it in her coat; asked no questions about the history; nodded to Jaina's 'Andorhal' and mounted; stopped the tally-man on the road and asked who runs the granaries; turned in the saddle at the farewell and asked Jaina what she had read; accepted the answer and put her heel to her horse.

Chapter 7: writes the cover pass under her own name, rank and seal (no other name that would get a mage and three bows through a gate). She does not use a cover name; the gate book records 'Escort, Farstriders, three' and copies her name.
Chapter 7: walks on past the barrel chalker without looking back at him.

Chapter 7: runs the questioning at the post in short questions (where sick, since when, why not taken); asks to see Fenner's herself; declines the 'it's covered' back approach in her head and goes anyway.

Chapter 7: splits the work by skill, not rank: Jaina, Corin and Lyriel to the sample room ('Proudmoore. The sample room. Take him.'); herself, Cyndia and Havel into the granary district; rendezvous 'When the Exchange rings the night shift.' Admits only to herself that it had been easier at Corley's with Jaina a shout away.
Chapter 7: leaves the dead drop in the wall untouched; follows the runner alone through Tenter Row and the back lane; refuses Havel's ladder offer ('I'll find my own').
Chapter 7: holds her tongue about Havel; watches his lane choices rather than his words.

Chapter 7: orders 'Tonight.' and drives her belt knife through her sheet to pin it; accepts Jaina's jaw-freeze plan (she had been about to ask); assigns Cyndia to the roofs across from Kett's loft and Lyriel to the Tenter Row bend; lets Havel's lads have the Hurdle Lane end ('Keep them there.'); tells Corin to stay behind Proudmoore and pinches out the candle.

abilitiesDemonstrated.ability: De-escalation: unarms herself, speaks only for one man's ears, concedes, tells a concrete story, gives him a way to keep face before his own people. Turns a levelled boar spear aside without raising her voice.
Supply-chain interrogation: reached the granary keeper and baker and extracted price, supplier, tally of loads and the supplier's description within a few hours; tests flour by pinch and finger.

Impossible shot: arrow through a running man's loose sleeve above the wrist and into the post behind him (pins the throwing arm) in the dark loft, with the lamp lit; follows at once to take the lamp and smother the oil (no one else sees her cross the loft).
Field intervention on a poisoning: pulls the dying lookout onto his side and sweeps his mouth with bare fingers while his teeth close on them.
Elite bowmanship: waited the shot, drew into the troll's half-stride on slick footing and hit under the arm.
Reads terrain and quarry behaviour (trolls run for water; chooses the stupid gap over suicidal slope).
Reads ward-stones by bare palm: a sound stone is warm inside, same at noon and midnight, with a steady hum; detected a hitched late beat and cold beneath the warmth that wardens and magisters missed.
Reads gait of a horse by ear (recognised the runner's Farstrider horse, long-legged with a drag on the near hind).
Commands a post by presence; reads a prisoner by posture.
Reads a hand-ruled map faster than its author: extended Jaina's ruled lines in her head and found where they close.

Command voice in a fight: single-word calls ('Front!', 'The stag!', 'Right!', 'Head.') that structure the action so the mage could 'draw the whole fight from those calls'; drops the lead doe with her first shot and puts an arrow through the heart of the second, which keeps running. Ordinary voice resumes at once ('Hold').
Field dressing and hunting craft: one long clean stroke opens the doe's belly; kneels in the ditch water as if it were not there.

Site reading: reads a sacked steading 'from the gate' (door broken, thatch fallen, people where they stood to fight or ran), so she can tell at once that Millhaven is a different thing (people left mid-routine at different hours, doors shut behind them, no blood, no dogs). Reads small details (drawknife laid squared, rag folded over a basin rim, dust on steel).

Tactical geometry in a village: perimeter and bridge hold, paired sweeps, covered sightlines for the mage's read, a staged ladder-and-hatch approach with Neral in front and an arrow on the string, a night watch that covers all four roads from the inn gallery.

Track-reading by depth and edge: measures groove depth against her first knuckle; distinguishes a tired drag (comes and goes with the lift and fall of the foot) from a constant toe-down weight; reads rain-rounded edges and a glazed bottom. Gets a count out of Cyndia's hazel-switch box method by letting the mage mark which prints are heavy.
Writes a clear field dispatch under bad conditions (a worn stub of lead failed; she switches to the mage's pen and Kirin Tor ink).

Reads a place by what has been done to it: the swept barn (corners, bare tie-beams, rectangles on the floor where sacks lay), the ash-pan curl still glowing, the shawl stepped over on the stair, the slumped-edge ruts on clay after rain. She decodes the wrongness, though she reads the stove one scene too late.

Archival tracking: reads a depot out-book, spots 'And.' in the margin and the short-rate 'own cart' lines, turns paper into a dated map; lays scraps out 'the way she would lay out arrowheads off a field, by kind'.
Cold tactical inference under fatigue: sees why the King's road is a trap of cleanliness, why an army is on the south road, and that whoever told the overseer would watch the road she took.
Chapter 6: fast camp read of a command structure and its blind side (who runs it, where messengers go, which way the pickets and archers face, what is unguarded on the road side).
Chapter 6: read of a commander's priorities before he spoke them, and the nerve to say it to his face in front of his staff, in a voice he could dismiss and did not.

Chapter 6: pattern memory for a phrase across places (the Millhaven carter's blessing identified in a stranger on a busy road); calming a frightened Thalassian horse with voice and hand in the language of the horse.

Chapter 7: reads a gate as ground and finds paper; reads the yard at Fenner's as hostile ground (trained waiting, sentries placed as she would place them); notices the runner's eyes-front walk past Havel; marks Havel's lane-steering and the bend in Tenter Row as she passes it.

Chapter 7: urban tail: matches the runner's pace at the lane's side, uses a wagon's high wheels and axle noise as cover, climbs a water butt and lean-to to the roofs, crosses roofs bent low keeping the ridge between herself and the street, and watches the loft through a knocked-out pane from behind a chimney stack. Reads the glove-removal discipline as proof the masked men protect themselves from the grain.

Chapter 7: sketches the picture in lead on the back of her sheet (square for Fenner's, box for the rope-walk, eight strokes, a single stroke on the wall at the lane mouth, a second square with five strokes and a ring for the crock) and mimes the glove removal to Jaina.

howSheAddressesOthers.pattern: Aloud: 'Mage.' (twice at the depot), 'Proudmoore. Read him.', 'Proudmoore. Barov.' and 'Mage, with me.' Never 'Jaina' aloud. Interior narration: 'the mage' every time in scenes 1 to 5 and the first half of the midnight scene; then at the fork, the line 'Jaina had been on her feet before the question was cold. / Jaina, then.' and from that point her interior calls her 'Jaina' (the first time ever). Is not yet spoken to her.
'Master Corley' (taken from Lyriel), once 'your clerk'; otherwise imperatives ('Their names.', 'Copy the short-rate lines out for me...').
'Cyndia.' / 'Lyriel.' curt first-name tasking; 'Lyriel, get the mage down.'
Bare first name (also the first word of her written dispatch: 'Lor'themar.' in Thalassian, no greeting).
'Mage' every time ('Mage. What you find, I want before dark.', 'Well, mage?', 'Mage. Will it hold?', 'Mage. Up.'); 'my mage' to Brask; never 'Jaina' or 'Proudmoore' aloud this chapter.

'Captain' (Brask, ever after the spear scene); 'Cyndia, with me.'; 'Lyriel. With the mage.' (first names, curt, repeating the orders 'Lyriel. With the mage. Cyndia, with me.' word-for-word at noon and dusk).

'Mage' as direct address throughout chapter 3 ('Mage. With me.', 'Mage. Up.'); 'Proudmoore' used twice at the well ('Proudmoore.' then '*Proudmoore!*') when the mage will not come up out of a read; narration and interiority use 'the mage' every time, never 'Jaina'; 'the prisoner' in status thoughts about custody.
'Cyndia' curt, no honorific, one-word orders ('Count.', 'Cyndia. Bring the lantern.', 'Cyndia. Wrap the mage's hands.').
First names, curt ('Neral, the horses into the inn yard', 'Lyriel to the top of the lane').
'The fourth' / 'the fourth ranger'; never named; no gendered pronoun used.
Does not name her (the girl has never given a name); thinks of her as 'the child', 'the girl', 'a human brat' (in her sneer about the Convocation's reaction).

'Mage' when speaking to her ('He has orcs in his hills, Mage. Make it short.', 'Give it here, Mage.', 'Mage. Did you read anything off him?'); 'Proudmoore' when speaking in front of Arthas or the sergeant, including to Jaina with Arthas in earshot ('Proudmoore rides under my escort.', 'He's going to write to his father, Proudmoore'). Never 'Jaina'.
'Your Highness', the two words 'perfectly level'. Does not use his name.

Aloud: 'Proudmoore. The sample room. Take him.' ('Proudmoore' in front of the others; no 'Mage' this chapter). Interior: 'Jaina' plainly ('Jaina could read the bags.', 'And Jaina was across the city by now') with one 'the mage' in passing ('the mage would get a bench in a hall'). Reliance not voiced.
No name aloud ('Take him.', 'Stay behind Proudmoore.'); interior 'the boy', 'the Dalaran boy'.
'Cyndia.' / 'Lyriel.' first names, orders by event; 'my ranger' to Havel for Cyndia ('Show my ranger the shed doors').

bodyLanguagePatterns.detail: Right hand closes into a fist without meaning to when the stone or the mage's claim is mentioned; she opens it and finds the cold still there. Rubs the palm against her thigh at the next stones.
Thumbs the knife edge out of habit after a kill; wipes blades on ferns twice; cleans and keeps her arrows.
Lifts two fingers off the reins as a farewell/acknowledgement to Lor'themar; raises a fist to halt the patrol.
Stands narrow-eyed into hard light; holds her tongue and lets a prisoner sit in silence to apply pressure.

Stands in the cell with her shadow over the prisoner; looks at Jaina's mouth; does not move until she moves 'first', half a step in, right hand flat on the wall a hand's breadth from the stone beside Jaina's head. Chin turns a fraction toward the door to give an order.

Does not turn her head when refusing; rides with her back to Jaina; checks each of her people one by one and the mage last, the way a quartermaster looks at a cracked crucible. Stops dead in the road before the staff hums, head turned toward the holly, bow in left hand and right hand on the fletching.
Wipes the knife on verge grass; turns her head to the road south and then the sky over the wood (reading weather and light) before ordering a hard ride.

Sits the mare through a spook and holds her 'by the knee and the mouth'; watches the mare's ears. Nocks an arrow when taking a side of the village; keeps her back to a wall or well-head and the bow in her hand; her hand goes to the string again and again on the gallery and she makes herself take it off. Whistles two short notes through two fingers to call rangers in.

Gives a child room: stands half in and half out of the doorway to watch the lane and the room, and 'gave Neral the room'; turns away from Neral's gentleness with the child ('Sylvanas turned away from it'); sets the toy wooden horse on the table out of habit (things on floors get trodden on in the dark).

Takes a mage by the wrist and pulls her hand up off a frozen road; steps back out of a doorway to give an order; wipes her palm down her thigh after touching mud; presses her ring into wax before it pools; unscrews and screws a tube cap; lays a hand flat on her mare's neck to take her pulse and her own calm.

Chapter 4: stops the line at the spear without a gesture, swings down and walks forward unarmed with her hands at her sides ('hands at her sides and nothing in them', repeated at the cage); stands close enough that Brask must lean in; at the chapel stands at the end of Elsie's bed with her back to the wall and the door at her left hand and reads the room like a wood; at the granary corner puts up a bare hand to stop everyone and points ('There. Stay.'); on the loft stair goes first with an arrow on the string and the bow low, planks making no sound; stands a step back from the cage bars with arms down; tries Tam's mouth on her knees; wipes her fingers on her coat; stays on the threshold with her left hand on the doorframe at night.

Chapter 5: puts the flat of her hand to her coat over the sacking square on the ride and takes it away; works her bitten fingers open and shut; holds the mage's reins at crossings and watches her face; had a hand 'ready' for the mage's elbow (the cliff-path habit) and did not need it; presses her finger on the Hollow Green bar until the nail whitens; pinches the candle out to protect Jaina's hair; kneels on bad knees to the stove; stands in the empty office with her hands at her sides; climbs the wall to take the watch; folds the sheet 'wrong' on new creases twice.

Chapter 6: faces the road ahead while Jaina talks, bow easy; lifts her chin to indicate the near side of the camp; sits her horse still to read it; gets down and stands at the stirrup; hands the paper up and passes the mare's rein to Cyndia; steps back; stands behind Jaina during the audience; studies Arthas 'long and steady, as he might have a boy across the practice yard who had read his feint'; steps round and takes the place where Arthas stood; holds out her hand for the sheet and refolds it herself when Jaina's fingers fail; gives a short nod; puts her horse across a stranger's path; turns right round in the saddle with one hand on her horse's rump and scans the full road; looks back a second time with Jaina.

Chapter 7: does not look back at the barrel chalker; stands at the corner behind a wagon watching the yard over the horses' backs; says nothing against Havel; draws an invisible glove off her hand finger by finger and drops it, to show Jaina the masked men's handling; pulls her belt knife and drives it through the sheet's corner into the table to stop it curling; pinches the candle out with her fingers to end the scene.

knowledge.detail: Has read the Farstrider file on Jaina Proudmoore last winter and wrote her off as a future nuisance.
Knows one stone on the southern track is wrong (late beat, cold under warmth) and that the same stone is circled on the mage's map.
Knows the magisters' wardens reported the ring stable in spring, 'in three different hands'.
Knows the prisoner's identity and that a human crossed two rings unfelt before dawn.

Does NOT know the cause (plague/leyline corruption), who sent the mage, or whether Antonidas knows. [Updated chapter 2: has been told 'nobody sent me', the Kirin Tor do not know, a note on Antonidas's desk.]

Knows the leyline map closes at Millhaven; knows the contamination is 'necromantic' per Jaina, that it is in living animals before death, and where it is strongest (staff points south toward the crossing). Does not say what she makes of it.

Chapter 3 holds: Millhaven's people got up from what they were doing at different hours and walked out; the whole village is soaked, the storehouse by the mill reads loudest but the mage will not call it the origin; the well water, the wheel-side lane prints and the drove-way prints carry it; horses (all of them, including hers) read clean; the lines at the crossing do not give a clean source-or-sink answer (north lines lag, east does not, west drowned out); the survivor girl's account: Missus Hale's baby sick first, then Mister Pell, then everyone coughing at the well; breath turned sweet ('pears gone brown') before the fever; Mam died (the shaving glass did not mist), got up in the dark; Da put her in the cellar and told her to bolt it 'not for anybody, not if it was him'; feet dragging past the slot, away from the mill toward Pell's, 'hundreds, all night, every night'; the newer grain seller, cheaper than Mister Hollis, caused a quarrel and visited the house in the last days, as did Gran Ottley and a tinker.

Chapter 3 also holds: at least sixty heavy marks, four and five abreast, went up the drove way (the 'cow way') north and a little east, toward the stones, away from the Pass road; none went through the gap down to the farm; no leader's track found; the Pass road south is clear; the settlements south are said to be still trading, with smoke in every chimney (carter).

Heard once: the newer grain seller (girl) and 'a young fellow... new man' with a grain cart (carter). She files the first as ordinary village gossip ('Every village south of the Pass had a new man with a cart once a season') and does not link the two.

Does NOT know: what raised the dead, who or what drives them, where the girl's father went, whether the carter is anything but a carter, whether grain matters, how far the contamination reaches south, or whether the farm family's cart ever reached Millhaven. She does not know Jaina's unspoken question from the Ch2 crest.

Chapter 4 holds (from what is shown): the sick village is Brask's, three days' cart from Andorhal; the granary keeper bought from a new man for three months, four loads, the last a fortnight ago; the bakehouse draws all its flour from the granary; the new man is young, civil, fair or brown-haired, good horse, from the west road, pays well, asked after the keeper's wife's leg; the loft held 'most of the last load' plus a hidden jar under a floorboard; Tam, the hoist-hand taken on at the back end of summer, was a lookout who died by poison sewn in his collar rather than talk; the sacks were stencilled ANDORHAL; the grain road leads south and west; Jaina's read: one flour, dose-dependent, in everyone's gut; she told Brask Millhaven and he believed it.

Chapter 4 does NOT show whether she links the new grain man to Millhaven's 'newer grain seller' and the carter; Jaina links them aloud only in thought and Sylvanas was present when the girl said it ('Sylvanas had stood half in the doorway of the end house while the girl talked'). She says 'On purpose.' but gives no name or theory.

Chapter 5: knows the grain is run through a regional network of at least 31 (Corley) to 53+ (slips) places with Andorhal at one end of every readable slip, that the free 'own cart' short-rate loads began at midsummer (Millhaven first), and that the east road is only just starting (nine of its ten short-rate loads in the last month). Knows the Barov name and a Barov seal (a shield with a device, melted) are on the paper at the river depot. Knows the overseer lied, burned the books and fled south with his wife; knows 'Tolliver and Sons' of Brill was a false lead (unverified either way). Knows a company of King's foot cut across for the hill road, that Prince Arthas has an army at Strahnbrad after orcs, and that army wagons run up the south road full and back empty. Does not know who runs it, whether Barov is guilty, or who tells the doors ahead of her.

Chapter 6: has now seen the Strahnbrad camp's posture first-hand (command tent central, riders east and back, east pickets doubled, a single sergeant and a hedge on the south-road side; archers on the earth bank above the stream facing away from the road; wagons filing in behind the cook-tents with nobody looking inside). Has met Arthas for the first time (not shown to have met before; 'she had never met Arthas', per Jaina). Heard him decline to act; heard Jaina's plain statement of the plague. Holds the evidence sheet again. Heard the farewell 'May the stars keep your road' a second time (Millhaven carter, then Andorhal tally-man), identified it aloud, and knows Jaina read nothing off him. Does not say anything about the other things she has been turning over (the empty wagon, the grain dust on the planks) in this chapter. Does not know the internment-camp night, or why Arthas used Jaina's name.

Chapter 7: Andorhal is a working city with a gate book and a chalker's count on top of the gate's; grain is spiked at the gate 'since the Exchange said'. Havel: street truth of Mill Lane, the same-week supplier change, loaders hired from outside who walk in pairs and sleep in the rope-walk. Corin: copied yard marks (forty-one), Dalaran ignoring him, the sample-room bags. Jaina (report): bags on copied marks are 'heavy', on true marks 'clean'; the poison is a thin coat worked onto grain by hand after dressing and before sewing; alone it does little, what it carries wakes inside whoever eats the bread; necromancy and alchemy both. Sylvanas's own sighting: eight sentries at Fenner's, a runner who drops into a wall crack, five masked contaminators at Kett's with a crock, protective gloves and washing. She does not know who sits above, whether she was seen by the window man, or what is in the crock.

backstory.detail: Put her palm to ward-stones since girlhood, riding the line behind her mother's rangers.
Was taught to finish a kill with a knife under the jaw before she could string a longbow.
Must sit a bench in the Convocation chamber at Sunfury Spire in formal greens.
Per Lyriel: she corrected the Ranger-Lord at midsummer in front of his own captains over a map of his own patrols, and he 'went red right up to here'. 'She does that to everyone.'

Has seen 'sacked towns' and 'a steading burned out by trolls' (she has drills for those), and Amani raids: 'After the Amani came through a steading she could read it from the gate.' Has seen dead villages 'before, cold hearths and the doors kicked in', but never one she sat through the night in.

Chapter 4 (hint only, via Jaina): carries herself in front of civilians as someone who has spoken to frightened farmers on a flat voice before, 'a woman telling him how far it was to the next ford'; no new backstory stated.

arc.lie: The south is not her problem; the border ends at her wards and magister work is magister work.
arc.truth: The threat does not respect her line, and the magisters' signatures do not match what a hand on the stone knows.
arc.currentPosition: SUPERSEDED by chapter 5 (see currentPositionNote). Chapter 4 (outside view only): the lie is fully gone: she walks into a Lordaeron village, claims the village's trust by her own method, and shuts the grain down on a mage's say-so. Her practical eye (supply, authority, fear) leads Jaina's laboratory reading by hours. No interior in this chapter; her trust in Jaina is shown by acts (let my mage see your sick, 'Can you leave them?', 'Will it hold?'), not words. Still 'Mage', still 'Ranger-General'.
arc.currentPositionNote: Authoritative chapter-5 position: Chapter 5 (full interior again): the lie is gone and the trust is practical: she uses Jaina's read to choose the road ('The south road. Heavy...'; 'How sure?' 'As sure as Brent's.') though she cannot verify it, and for the first time thinks 'Jaina' (interior only), after the mage is faster to correct her own marks than any Silvermoon magister. Her pride takes a hit (the overseer day), and she learns to distrust fast, polite answers. Does not give praise or warmth; the 'No.' to a re-read is trust spent, not softness. 'Expect them to get in the way' / 'Then I'll have to show it to them.' / 'You'll have to. I can't see it either.' is the first admitted dependency.
arc.previousPosition_chapter3: Chapter 3: lie broken from the inside. Decides to ride on south after the border is warned, and names the reason as 'the trail', not the mage. Stops treating the mage's read as optional (asks the mage to sort the prints; waits for her well and storehouse reads; lets her refusal to call a source stand), but does not trust her: still thinks of her as 'the prisoner' and the one 'who knows where to go'. Still carries the border as her own concern (dispatch, wardens, the Convocation's arithmetic) while the south pulls at her.
arc.currentPositionNote_chapter6: Chapter 6 (outside view only): the Ch5 position stands and is vindicated, not celebrated. She calls Arthas to his face, names him a good commander with the wrong war for this, and sets the plague as 'ours'. Her tie to Jaina is working, not warm: she takes the sheet back, asks what Jaina read, and rides on at her word. The farewell has become a mark she carries as 'wrong, not yet a pattern'.
arc.currentPositionNote_chapter7: Chapter 7 (own POV): arrives treating Andorhal as a hunt (weak point, watch pattern); the gate answers with paper and the district answers with half a picture. The full picture only holds when Jaina's half (sample-room bags, the coat on the grain) and her own (the eight, the runner, Kett's loft) lie side by side; the raid exists only because both exist. She thinks 'Jaina' and relies on her without saying so; aloud she is still 'Proudmoore'. Her bias (impatience with slow humans) sits beside a real unease about Havel and she acts on neither.
